   160	---
   161	
   162	# AGMSG-TASK dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01 — INV-6 reset of a01 on tools/worker-write-boundary-a01, seat a010; plan 024 P1-15 under D-024-17, D-024-19, D-024-20, D-024-21 and D-024-23
   163	
   164	## Goal
   165	
   166	This is the amendment-1 text of the task dispatched at 2026-10-19T05:42Z (the ninth-round text that passed its pre-dispatch security review). Amendment 1 folds in two interpretation notes the worker needed (the inherited make format clause; the portable tracked `.claude/settings.json` with host-specific paths only in the rendered guard) and removes the Codex worker profile item (a Codex seat edits no Codex-boundary source; it becomes the separate Claude-seat task dotfiles-T133-codex-worker-network-a01). Everything else is the dispatched text in meaning; the branch, the eight green tests and the fixtures stay; the worker swaps the task copy to this text at its next push.
   167	
   168	The host is not a security boundary between seats sharing one OS user. gh keys Keychain credentials by host and user, so a worker running as the same macOS user can read the orchestrator's token regardless of `GH_CONFIG_DIR`. Prevention of a worker-initiated merge requires a separate OS user or host under D-024-23's future P1-16, which the operator decides whether to pursue. Until then the GitHub boundary is detection, not prevention. The regime detects missing acceptance or gate-passage evidence in the next records PR, not at main-push time, because the records reach main only with that boundary PR. On a PR touching `.orchestration/acceptance/**`, the regime job checks every main merge commit since the previous boundary for its corresponding acceptance record with gate-passage evidence and fails the PR when one is missing. P1-11 owns implementation of that check; this task states section 5.14 item 0's detection rule. Approvals and gate evidence of record are read from GitHub at a SHA through its API inside the sandbox. Host-local controls reduce accidental and injected damage without establishing isolation from a malicious same-UID process.
   169	
   170	This task implements section 5.14 items 1, 9 and 10 through a dedicated Claude worker configuration directory, static Edit deny rules on trusted paths and worktree configuration, managed sandbox enforcement, guarded project hooks, hook interpreter and PATH bindings, private worker caches and the rule that worker commands run inside their sandbox. Every Claude seat has `sandbox.failIfUnavailable: true`.
   171	
   172	The administrative managed policy is shared by every Claude seat. Its Herdr socket allowance and three control-plane exclusions remain available to workers as well as the orchestrator. Empty arrays in worker user settings do not subtract these managed entries. Their availability is a residual under item 0, and the worker execution rule supplies no authorization to use them outside the sandbox.
   173	
   174	[memory:decision] D-024-20 makes this task the dispatch prerequisite of P1-14 a05, P1-10 a02, audit-pool-a02 and P1-6. The orchestrator places this task in their `after:` fields before dispatch. This task has `after: []`. A Codex seat performs these Claude configuration edits under the routing rule, including the Worker Playbook step 4 sentence permitted by plan 021 step 8.3. This Codex seat edits no Codex-boundary source.
   175	
   176	The design source is `.orchestration/plans/024-design-quality.md` section 5.14 items 0 through 10. D-024-21, D-024-23 and the amended items 0, 1 and 8 govern this revision. D-024-22's proposed gh credential separation is superseded. The acceptance record preserves documentation facts and earlier proposals as history.
   177	
   178	The third C-80 text review is `.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-ecc7ab5.md.last.md`. Its five P1 findings remain recorded. The retained mechanisms are documented symlink-aware deny rules, approval reads outside the local object database, hook interpreter bindings and runtime hook failure policy.
   179	
   180	The fourth C-80 text review is `.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8d42532.md.last.md`. Its six P1 findings remain recorded. The retained mechanisms are the static manifest deny inventory, protection of the orchestrator worklog and cache, narrow home denies around writable agmsg stores, correct linked-worktree hook placement and fixed hook-runtime PATH.
   181	
   182	The fifth C-80 text review is `.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md.last.md`. Its three P1 findings remain recorded. This revision removes the gh credential-separation mechanism, records the upstream agmsg store-driver residual and moves sandbox enforcement into administrative managed settings.
   183	
   184	The file-tool rule is the documented sentence, “Deny rules: apply when either the requested path or the file it resolves to matches.” Edit and Write refuse a requested file that is itself a symlink. Directory symlinks are subject to resolved-target permission checks, and the tools check the resolved location again when opening the approved file. These documented checks reduce redirection risk without establishing an atomic host security boundary against concurrent same-UID changes. [Claude permission reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#symlinks)
   185	
   186	The 2026-10-19T03:45:06Z sandbox probe ran `gh api repos/mryfmo/dotfiles --jq .name` and returned `dotfiles`. The recorded sandbox proxy used CONNECT without TLS interception, and gh read the Keychain token. This historical observation confirms neither credential separation nor final-head deployment readiness.
   187	
   188	The documentation facts recorded at 03:2xZ establish that Edit denies also affect the Bash sandbox, hooks reload during a session and an unavailable sandbox is fail-open by default. D-024-21's 04:0xZ decision establishes the dedicated Claude configuration mechanism, directory-specific Claude credentials, symlink coverage and `onFailure: "block"` support. These Claude credentials do not separate gh Keychain access.
   189	
   190	The settings documentation states, “In a worktree, it uses the file at the main checkout’s root.” Linked-worktree sessions therefore load the main checkout's `.claude/settings.local.json`. Worker hooks belong in `~/.claude-worker/settings.json`, and the main checkout's local hooks also receive the orchestrator-only guard. [Claude local settings reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings#where-claude-code-keeps-the-local-file-in-a-git-repository)
   191	
   192	## Files
   193	
   194	1. `home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml` remains the source of agent policy and model profiles.
   195	
   196	   The manifest names `orchestrator_checkout` as the anchored primary checkout and supplies trusted deployment bindings for the guard, hook scripts and absolute interpreters. These bindings resolve outside worker worktrees and executable caches. Worker cwd, tool input, worktree configuration and inherited command variables do not select them. The manifest also supplies the trusted bindings from which the render resolves the absolute directories holding `ruff`, `prettier` and `terminal-browser`, without using mise shims.
   197	
   198	   The manifest defines a separate Claude worker settings output at `home/.chezmoitemplates/claude-worker-settings.json` and an administrative managed-settings output at `home/.chezmoitemplates/claude-managed-settings.json`. The worker configuration directory is `~/.claude-worker`. The launcher passes its expanded absolute path as `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.
   199	
   200	   A static `trusted_paths:` list names every protected top-level path of the anchored checkout and the protected home paths. It explicitly includes `<anchored-checkout>/.agents/worklog/**` and `<anchored-checkout>/.agents/worklog/uv-cache/**`. The `.claude` entries protect tracked contents and the main checkout's `.claude/settings.local.json` without denying the whole `.claude/worktrees/` tree. The list explicitly names directory targets and descendant patterns where both are required.
   201	
   202	   Separate worker Edit denies protect `//<anchored-checkout>/.claude/worktrees/*/.claude/**` and `//<anchored-checkout>/.claude/worktrees/*/.mcp.json`. The `.claude` directory target is also protected. Ordinary worktree source files and the per-seat cache remain outside these configuration denies.
   203	
   204	   The home-path denies are `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml`, `~/.agents/model-profiles.env`, `~/.agents/skills/**/scripts/**`, `~/.agents/skills/**/SKILL.md`, `~/.agents/skills/agmsg/plugins/**`, `~/.agents/skills/agmsg/db/trusted-plugins`, `~/.claude/**`, `~/.claude-worker/**`, `~/.local/bin/**`, `~/.local/share/**`, `~/.local/state/**`, `~/.local/share/mise/**`, `~/.config/**`, `~/.cache/uv/**` and `~/.local/share/uv/**`. No blanket deny on `~/.agents/**` or `~/.local/**` replaces this list.
   205	
   206	   The agmsg store paths `~/.agents/skills/agmsg/db`, `~/.agents/skills/agmsg/teams`, `~/.agents/skills/agmsg/run` and `~/.agents/skills/agmsg/ext-tools` remain writable. Deny patterns cover neither these directory targets nor their descendants except the file `~/.agents/skills/agmsg/db/trusted-plugins`. Edit denies merge into the sandbox configuration, so Bash writes to that file and `~/.agents/skills/agmsg/plugins/**` are refused too. Their influence on installed delivery-script driver and plugin selection remains the separately owned agmsg residual.
   207	
   208	   The orchestrator retains its existing permissions, cache allowances and hook functions within the administrative managed policy. Its user baseline receives `failIfUnavailable: true`, `onFailure: "block"` on its hooks and the interpreter and PATH bindings below. Its exclusion entries match the three control-plane entries specified below; the former Linux `gh *` exclusion is removed.
   209	
   210	   The worker user policy contains no excluded commands and sets `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false`. It contains no Herdr socket allowance and no allow-all Unix socket switch. Its sandbox is enabled and has `failIfUnavailable: true`. Shared managed entries remain effective despite these empty worker arrays.
   211	
   212	   Worker `sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite` contains only the existing agmsg store paths and per-seat cache paths. The worktree is the project root and supplies its ordinary project write root. Shared uv and mise write allowances are not copied into worker settings.
   213	
   214	   Existing model selections, Codex worker profile values, Codex sandbox and approval arguments and Codex shared Git grants retain their meaning and remain unchanged. The deterministic Codex permgate rule that stops approving sandbox escapes is an operator step.
   215	
   216	2. `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` renders the distinct orchestrator user, worker user and administrative managed baselines from the manifest.
   217	
   218	   The trusted-path deny inventory is rendered from the static `trusted_paths:` list. Rendering performs no Git object traversal, `git ls-tree` enumeration or tracked-path discovery. Worker-writable refs, replacement refs and objects do not determine the list.
   219	
   220	   Anchored checkout rules use absolute `//` permission patterns. Rendering includes the explicitly listed trusted paths themselves and their descendants. It emits no checkout-wide parent deny that defeats ordinary worktree writes. The separate worktree-configuration denies remain present.
   221	
   222	   Edit denies cover Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit through Claude's permission system. Requested-path and resolved-target matching supply the documented symlink coverage. The generator creates no `executable_worker-write-boundary.py` or replacement PreToolUse path validator.
   223	
   224	   Every direct Git verification introduced or changed by this task follows section 5.14 item 2. It begins with `env -i`, uses the selected absolute Git executable and an explicit `-C`, sets `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, and supplies `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false -c protocol.allow=never -c protocol.https.allow=always`. Diff and show also use `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv` and `-c core.attributesFile=/dev/null -c core.sshCommand=false`.
   225	
   226	   The private executable-link directory contains only links to selected absolute trusted binaries. Rendering rejects missing bindings, worker-controlled executable paths, shims, empty PATH entries and relative PATH entries. Python invocations use `-I`. Hook execution uses the role-specific pinned PATH bindings specified below. The render test asserts that `ruff`, `prettier` and `terminal-browser` resolve under the rendered orchestrator tool PATH on the rendering host and that no entry of that PATH is a shims directory.
   227	
   228	   `tests/unit/test_generate_agent_configs.py::GenerateAgentConfigsTest::test_worker_deny_inventory_is_static_and_matches_manifest` asserts that the rendered list equals the manifest entry after trusted anchor and home expansion. It explicitly asserts the rendered home-path deny patterns `~/.local/share/**` and `~/.local/state/**`, including the application code under `~/.local/share` used by `~/.local/bin` wrappers such as `terminal-browser`. It reads the filesystem of the test's own checkout and asserts that every tracked top-level source path is represented. It invokes no Git command to discover those paths.
   229	
   230	   The inventory fixtures cover files, directories, `.claude` children, the main-local settings file, ordinary worktree writes, both worktree-configuration patterns, an anchor containing spaces and both explicit worklog patterns. Adding a top-level source path without a manifest entry makes the coverage assertion fail. Planted Git environment and replacement-ref fixtures leave rendering unchanged.
   231	
   232	   `tests/unit/test_claude_worker_settings.py::ClaudeWorkerSettingsTest::test_worker_denies_leave_agmsg_stores_writable` asserts the rendered deny patterns `~/.agents/skills/agmsg/plugins/**` and `~/.agents/skills/agmsg/db/trusted-plugins` and verifies that the four store directories `db`, `teams`, `run` and `ext-tools` and their descendant fixtures remain writable except that one file.
   233	
   234	3. `home/.chezmoitemplates/claude-settings-managed.json` remains the orchestrator user baseline.
   235	
   236	   The existing `home/dot_claude/modify_private_settings.json` continues to render the orchestrator's `~/.claude/settings.json`. That modify script is not imported into the dedicated worker renderer and remains outside `allowed_files`.
   237	
   238	   This existing template's name does not make it administrative managed settings. The new `claude-managed-settings.json` template supplies that separate scope.
   239	
   240	   The orchestrator retains its current user policy content apart from `failIfUnavailable: true`, `onFailure: "block"`, the required interpreter and PATH bindings and alignment of exclusions with the three control-plane entries. Worker-specific Edit denies and restricted worker cache allowances do not enter this baseline. Administrative sandbox requirements apply to the orchestrator as well as workers.
   241	
   242	   Every generated hook entry carries `onFailure: "block"`. Every generated command hook starts with `/usr/bin/env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME="$HOME" LANG=C.UTF-8 TERM=dumb CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}" CLAUDE_ENV_FILE="${CLAUDE_ENV_FILE}"` before its trusted installed entrypoint. The prefix re-exports HOME from the launcher environment before any HOME-relative entrypoint path. Host-specific interpreter, private-link-directory, anchored-checkout and tool-directory bindings remain in the per-host rendered guard and rendered worker settings. The formatter and project-map hooks run through the installed orchestrator-only guard and receive the role-specific pinned PATH specified below. Merge evidence identifies hooks appended by the existing modify script and distinguishes them from generated baseline entries. The report accounts for the effective deployed hook set without equating baseline coverage with coverage of runtime-added entries.
   243	
   244	   `tests/unit/test_claude_settings_merge.py::ClaudeSettingsMergeTest::test_orchestrator_settings_keep_existing_policy` compares the merged policy with the preceding baseline and accounts for the specified changes. Repeated merging remains idempotent and preserves unrelated settings.
   245	
   246	4. `home/.chezmoitemplates/claude-worker-settings.json` is the dedicated worker user baseline.
   247	
   248	   It renders the static trusted-path Edit denies, the worktree `.claude` and `.mcp.json` Edit denies, retained native merge denials, empty user `excludedCommands`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false`, restricted `allowWrite`, no user Herdr socket allowance and `failIfUnavailable: true` for both Darwin and Linux.
   249	
   250	   Its hooks are limited to agmsg delivery. It contains no formatter, project-map, permgate, orchestrator attachment, Herdr state or worker-write-boundary hook. Tracked project hooks and main-checkout local hooks still load and receive the guard described below.
   251	
   252	   Every worker hook entry carries `onFailure: "block"`. Every command starts with `/usr/bin/env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME="$HOME" LANG=C.UTF-8 TERM=dumb CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}" CLAUDE_ENV_FILE="${CLAUDE_ENV_FILE}" AGMSG_RESOLVE_PROJECT=0` before the selected absolute shell interpreter and absolute installed agmsg script path. The prefix also re-exports `AGMSG_STORAGE_PATH` when it is set in the launcher environment. Project resolution from a writable `run/proj.<pid>.project` marker remains disabled, so delivery retains the explicit worker path. Descendants inherit this PATH.
   253	
   254	   The worker baseline does not copy the orchestrator's plugins, credential files or current hook arrays. .orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-ecc7ab5.md:4835:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:219](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:219) Absolute hook entrypoints do not bind their descendants: retained `herdr-agent-state.sh:25` invokes bare `python3`, while delivery invokes scripts with `/usr/bin/env bash` shebangs; the specified launcher captures and tracked-hook tests miss these unsandboxed, PATH-resolved executions on this shim-first host. [Mise shim resolution](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/shims.html).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-ecc7ab5.md:4837:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:84](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:84) The table omits the retained Herdr socket capability (`agent-config.yaml:325`): a sandboxed client can request terminal execution through the host server, whose existing driver uses `pane run`; refusing excluded command names does not restrict socket RPCs or the resulting host execution. [Unix-socket escape risk](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#security-limitations).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-ecc7ab5.md:4839:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:275](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:275) Startup validation does not mitigate a later hook timeout or termination, which permits the protected action; Python exit-2 tests therefore leave enforcement fail-open, although Claude provides runtime-level `onFailure: "block"` starting with v2.1.295. .orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-435275a.md:14:Pre-dispatch security review (read-only, security profile) of the task text .orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md and its threat_table, before any implementation exists. Judge the design the text states: can the controls it names bind what actually executes on this host (mise shims first on PATH, same-user worker processes, gh outside the sandbox on Linux, symlinks and case-insensitive filesystems, inherited GIT_* environment)? Check every threat row: a closed row whose named test cannot close it, a residual row whose control does not mitigate the risk, a missing row for a file or non-path control, and any gap of the class decision-not-bound-to-execution (a decision made on text or on a validated copy while the execution resolves binaries, files or ledgers from an attacker-influenced place). Read the related acceptance records and reviews the text cites for context. Report each finding as [P0-P3] <confidence> <file:line> <one line>; findings are input for the orchestrator, who decides. .orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-435275a.md:4931:- 2026-10-19T03:24:11Z: C-80 review of the text (`.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8bac9e5.md`): `Verdict: incorrect`, seven P1, one P2: (1) the gh wrapper forwards argv verbatim, so `gh repo clone … -- --config core.sshCommand=<exe>` runs worker code outside the sandbox → the wrapper allows an explicit subcommand list and refuses `--` passthrough and config-carrying forms; (2) a bash wrapper reads BASH_ENV before `env -i` (probe confirmed) → the wrapper is Python under an absolute `-I` interpreter path rendered from the trusted root; (3) project hooks execute the worktree's `.claude/hooks/contextdb_hook.py` through bare `python3` and the format hooks resolve tools through shims → worker seats run no project hooks (a factual check of the settings switch is pending with the Claude Code docs); (4) Codex workers share `.git/objects` and `.git/refs` writes (herdr-agents:439), so `origin/main` can be replaced after a fetch → design 5.14 item 8 now binds the committed ledger to the sha `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` returns (amended 03:2xZ); (5) `git ls-tree` enumeration needs the sanitized git environment; (6) the reviewer states Edit deny rules also enter the Bash sandbox configuration, which would block the orchestrator's sandboxed record writes under `.orchestration/**` → a factual check pending; (7) `failIfUnavailable: false` lets a seat run unsandboxed when Linux dependencies are missing → `true` for worker seats; (8) P2: symlink and case-alias identity tests missing. Five facts are being verified against the Claude Code documentation before the revision (excludedCommands matching, hooks switches and capture, Edit denies vs sandbox, failIfUnavailable, Edit rule scope and path forms).

.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-e5d1b57.md:2602:- 2026-10-19T03:24:11Z: C-80 review of the text (`.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8bac9e5.md`): `Verdict: incorrect`, seven P1, one P2: (1) the gh wrapper forwards argv verbatim, so `gh repo clone … -- --config core.sshCommand=<exe>` runs worker code outside the sandbox → the wrapper allows an explicit subcommand list and refuses `--` passthrough and config-carrying forms; (2) a bash wrapper reads BASH_ENV before `env -i` (probe confirmed) → the wrapper is Python under an absolute `-I` interpreter path rendered from the trusted root; (3) project hooks execute the worktree's `.claude/hooks/contextdb_hook.py` through bare `python3` and the format hooks resolve tools through shims → worker seats run no project hooks (a factual check of the settings switch is pending with the Claude Code docs); (4) Codex workers share `.git/objects` and `.git/refs` writes (herdr-agents:439), so `origin/main` can be replaced after a fetch → design 5.14 item 8 now binds the committed ledger to the sha `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` returns (amended 03:2xZ); (5) `git ls-tree` enumeration needs the sanitized git environment; (6) the reviewer states Edit deny rules also enter the Bash sandbox configuration, which would block the orchestrator's sandboxed record writes under `.orchestration/**` → a factual check pending; (7) `failIfUnavailable: false` lets a seat run unsandboxed when Linux dependencies are missing → `true` for worker seats; (8) P2: symlink and case-alias identity tests missing. Five facts are being verified against the Claude Code documentation before the revision (excludedCommands matching, hooks switches and capture, Edit denies vs sandbox, failIfUnavailable, Edit rule scope and path forms).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-e5d1b57.md:2631:- 2026-10-19T06:23Z: the amendment-1 text (the review-profile a02 output re-targeted to a01: the inherited make format clause, the portable tracked settings.json with host paths only in the rendered guard, the Codex network_access item removed to the Claude-seat task dotfiles-T133-codex-worker-network-a01) installed; checker OK; its C-80 review started 06:23Z; dispatch to a010 on correct.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-e5d1b57.md:2636:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:273](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:273) The race acceptance rests on a false premise: a sandboxed worker can swap an allowed directory for a symlink after validation, causing the unsandboxed file tool to overwrite a trusted path that the worker cannot write directly; static path tests cannot close this boundary.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-e5d1b57.md:2638:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:80](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:80) Remote SHA pinning and `--no-replace-objects` do not authenticate the writable object database: replacing an intermediate tree object can redirect ledger lookup to an attacker’s valid blob because that traversal does not verify the intermediate object’s content hash. [Git tree traversal](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.51.0/tree-walk.c), [object reading](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.51.0/odb.c).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-e5d1b57.md:2640:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:219](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:219) Absolute hook entrypoints do not bind their descendants: retained `herdr-agent-state.sh:25` invokes bare `python3`, while delivery invokes scripts with `/usr/bin/env bash` shebangs; the specified launcher captures and tracked-hook tests miss these unsandboxed, PATH-resolved executions on this shim-first host. [Mise shim resolution](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/shims.html).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-e5d1b57.md:2642:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:84](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:84) The table omits the retained Herdr socket capability (`agent-config.yaml:325`): a sandboxed client can request terminal execution through the host server, whose existing driver uses `pane run`; refusing excluded command names does not restrict socket RPCs or the resulting host execution. [Unix-socket escape risk](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#security-limitations).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-e5d1b57.md:2644:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:275](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:275) Startup validation does not mitigate a later hook timeout or termination, which permits the protected action; Python exit-2 tests therefore leave enforcement fail-open, although Claude provides runtime-level `onFailure: "block"` starting with v2.1.295. [Hook failure control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#block-the-action-when-a-hook-fails).

.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md:2350:- 2026-10-19T03:24:11Z: C-80 review of the text (`.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8bac9e5.md`): `Verdict: incorrect`, seven P1, one P2: (1) the gh wrapper forwards argv verbatim, so `gh repo clone … -- --config core.sshCommand=<exe>` runs worker code outside the sandbox → the wrapper allows an explicit subcommand list and refuses `--` passthrough and config-carrying forms; (2) a bash wrapper reads BASH_ENV before `env -i` (probe confirmed) → the wrapper is Python under an absolute `-I` interpreter path rendered from the trusted root; (3) project hooks execute the worktree's `.claude/hooks/contextdb_hook.py` through bare `python3` and the format hooks resolve tools through shims → worker seats run no project hooks (a factual check of the settings switch is pending with the Claude Code docs); (4) Codex workers share `.git/objects` and `.git/refs` writes (herdr-agents:439), so `origin/main` can be replaced after a fetch → design 5.14 item 8 now binds the committed ledger to the sha `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` returns (amended 03:2xZ); (5) `git ls-tree` enumeration needs the sanitized git environment; (6) the reviewer states Edit deny rules also enter the Bash sandbox configuration, which would block the orchestrator's sandboxed record writes under `.orchestration/**` → a factual check pending; (7) `failIfUnavailable: false` lets a seat run unsandboxed when Linux dependencies are missing → `true` for worker seats; (8) P2: symlink and case-alias identity tests missing. Five facts are being verified against the Claude Code documentation before the revision (excludedCommands matching, hooks switches and capture, Edit denies vs sandbox, failIfUnavailable, Edit rule scope and path forms).

.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md:2379:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:273](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:273) The race acceptance rests on a false premise: a sandboxed worker can swap an allowed directory for a symlink after validation, causing the unsandboxed file tool to overwrite a trusted path that the worker cannot write directly; static path tests cannot close this boundary.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md:2381:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:80](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:80) Remote SHA pinning and `--no-replace-objects` do not authenticate the writable object database: replacing an intermediate tree object can redirect ledger lookup to an attacker’s valid blob because that traversal does not verify the intermediate object’s content hash. [Git tree traversal](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.51.0/tree-walk.c), [object reading](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.51.0/odb.c).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md:2383:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:219](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:219) Absolute hook entrypoints do not bind their descendants: retained `herdr-agent-state.sh:25` invokes bare `python3`, while delivery invokes scripts with `/usr/bin/env bash` shebangs; the specified launcher captures and tracked-hook tests miss these unsandboxed, PATH-resolved executions on this shim-first host. [Mise shim resolution](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/shims.html).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md:2385:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:84](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:84) The table omits the retained Herdr socket capability (`agent-config.yaml:325`): a sandboxed client can request terminal execution through the host server, whose existing driver uses `pane run`; refusing excluded command names does not restrict socket RPCs or the resulting host execution. [Unix-socket escape risk](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#security-limitations).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md:2387:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:275](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:275) Startup validation does not mitigate a later hook timeout or termination, which permits the protected action; Python exit-2 tests therefore leave enforcement fail-open, although Claude provides runtime-level `onFailure: "block"` starting with v2.1.295. [Hook failure control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#block-the-action-when-a-hook-fails).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md:2392:Verdict: incorrect- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:131](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:131) No threat row or control separates worker GitHub credentials from the orchestrator’s: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` does not isolate gh authentication, so a worker with the shared credential can call the merge API through permitted sandbox networking; GitHub cannot enforce the claimed seat identity distinction. [gh credential selection](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_environment).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md:2394:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:165](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:165) The deny inventory trusts the same worker-writable Git objects and refs rejected for ledger authority: planted replacement refs can make `git ls-tree` omit protected paths, and neither `env -i` nor the prescribed flags authenticate that enumeration; the named fixtures omit this attack. [Git replacement semantics](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-replace).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md:2396:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:267](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:267) The “protected” orchestrator cache is absent from the specified deny inventory: checkout-local `.agents/worklog/uv-cache` is gitignored, `.agents` is absent from the tracked top-level tree, and `~/.agents/**` names a different directory; `--offline` does not prevent execution of poisoned local cache content.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md:2398:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:169](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:169) Denying all `~/.agents/**` also denies the required agmsg `db`, `teams`, `run` and `ext-tools` writes beneath it, contradicting line 159’s allowances and preventing sandboxed worker messaging; render tests that merely assert both lists cannot establish a functioning policy. [Combined sandbox enforcement](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#how-sandboxing-relates-to-permissions).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md:2400:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:235](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:235) Preparing worktree-local delivery settings misses the main checkout’s local settings, which linked-worktree sessions also load and which currently contain unguarded agmsg hooks bound to the main project; dedicated user settings and tracked-hook guards therefore do not establish the promised effective hook set. [Local settings resolution](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings#where-claude-code-keeps-the-local-file-in-a-git-repository).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md:2402:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:251](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:251) Absolute entrypoint interpreters cannot satisfy the descendant contract while installed agmsg scripts remain unchanged: `session-start.sh:59` directly executes `identities.sh`, whose shebang is `/usr/bin/env bash`; the text supplies no hook-runtime PATH binding that prevents this unsandboxed descendant from resolving through the host’s shims. [Shim resolution](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/shims.html).

.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md:3877:Pre-dispatch security review (read-only, security profile) of the task text .orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md and its threat_table, before any implementation exists. Check every threat row: a closed row whose named test cannot close it, a residual row whose control does not mitigate the risk, a missing row for a file or non-path control, and any gap of the class decision-not-bound-to-execution (a decision made on text or on a validated copy while the execution resolves binaries, files or ledgers from an attacker-influenced place). Read the related acceptance records and reviews the text cites for context. Report each finding as [P0-P3] <confidence> <file:line> <one line>; findings are input for the orchestrator, who decides. End with exactly one line: Verdict: correct or Verdict: incorrect.

.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8d42532.md:1155:- 2026-10-19T03:24:11Z: C-80 review of the text (`.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8bac9e5.md`): `Verdict: incorrect`, seven P1, one P2: (1) the gh wrapper forwards argv verbatim, so `gh repo clone … -- --config core.sshCommand=<exe>` runs worker code outside the sandbox → the wrapper allows an explicit subcommand list and refuses `--` passthrough and config-carrying forms; (2) a bash wrapper reads BASH_ENV before `env -i` (probe confirmed) → the wrapper is Python under an absolute `-I` interpreter path rendered from the trusted root; (3) project hooks execute the worktree's `.claude/hooks/contextdb_hook.py` through bare `python3` and the format hooks resolve tools through shims → worker seats run no project hooks (a factual check of the settings switch is pending with the Claude Code docs); (4) Codex workers share `.git/objects` and `.git/refs` writes (herdr-agents:439), so `origin/main` can be replaced after a fetch → design 5.14 item 8 now binds the committed ledger to the sha `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` returns (amended 03:2xZ); (5) `git ls-tree` enumeration needs the sanitized git environment; (6) the reviewer states Edit deny rules also enter the Bash sandbox configuration, which would block the orchestrator's sandboxed record writes under `.orchestration/**` → a factual check pending; (7) `failIfUnavailable: false` lets a seat run unsandboxed when Linux dependencies are missing → `true` for worker seats; (8) P2: symlink and case-alias identity tests missing. Five facts are being verified against the Claude Code documentation before the revision (excludedCommands matching, hooks switches and capture, Edit denies vs sandbox, failIfUnavailable, Edit rule scope and path forms).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8d42532.md:1166:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:273](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:273) The race acceptance rests on a false premise: a sandboxed worker can swap an allowed directory for a symlink after validation, causing the unsandboxed file tool to overwrite a trusted path that the worker cannot write directly; static path tests cannot close this boundary.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8d42532.md:1168:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:80](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:80) Remote SHA pinning and `--no-replace-objects` do not authenticate the writable object database: replacing an intermediate tree object can redirect ledger lookup to an attacker’s valid blob because that traversal does not verify the intermediate object’s content hash. [Git tree traversal](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.51.0/tree-walk.c), [object reading](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.51.0/odb.c).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8d42532.md:1170:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:219](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:219) Absolute hook entrypoints do not bind their descendants: retained `herdr-agent-state.sh:25` invokes bare `python3`, while delivery invokes scripts with `/usr/bin/env bash` shebangs; the specified launcher captures and tracked-hook tests miss these unsandboxed, PATH-resolved executions on this shim-first host. [Mise shim resolution](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/shims.html).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8d42532.md:1172:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:84](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:84) The table omits the retained Herdr socket capability (`agent-config.yaml:325`): a sandboxed client can request terminal execution through the host server, whose existing driver uses `pane run`; refusing excluded command names does not restrict socket RPCs or the resulting host execution. [Unix-socket escape risk](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#security-limitations).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8d42532.md:1174:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:275](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:275) Startup validation does not mitigate a later hook timeout or termination, which permits the protected action; Python exit-2 tests therefore leave enforcement fail-open, although Claude provides runtime-level `onFailure: "block"` starting with v2.1.295. [Hook failure control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#block-the-action-when-a-hook-fails).

.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8d42532.md:1673:- [P2] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:171](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:171) The executable-boundary closure test covers a PATH shim but never a selected absolute path resolving through symlinks or case aliases into a worker root; it cannot establish §5.14.3’s filesystem-identity requirement on this host, where `.git` and `.GIT` have the same inode.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8d42532.md:1678:Verdict: incorrect- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:174](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:174) Worker identity depends on mutable event `cwd`: a worker can `cd` outside the worker root and receive the nonworker “no decision” result; identity and allowed roots must remain bound to the launched seat. .orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8d42532.md:1680:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:186](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:186) The existing-hook residual provides no effective mitigation: `.claude/settings.json` executes worker-writable `scripts/agent-stop-gate.sh`, while formatting runs PATH-resolved Prettier against worker-controlled JavaScript configuration; protecting `.claude` settings does not bind the executed code. .orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-1ae3138.md:14:Pre-dispatch security review (read-only, security profile) of the task text .orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md and its threat_table, before any implementation exists. Judge the design the text states: can the controls it names bind what actually executes on this host (mise shims first on PATH, same-user worker processes, gh outside the sandbox on Linux, symlinks and case-insensitive filesystems, inherited GIT_* environment)? Check every threat row: a closed row whose named test cannot close it, a residual row whose control does not mitigate the risk, a missing row for a file or non-path control, and any gap of the class decision-not-bound-to-execution (a decision made on text or on a validated copy while the execution resolves binaries, files or ledgers from an attacker-influenced place). Read the related acceptance records and reviews the text cites for context. Report each finding as [P0-P3] <confidence> <file:line> <one line>; findings are input for the orchestrator, who decides. End with exactly one line: Verdict: correct or Verdict: incorrect.

.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-67415f5.md.last.md:3:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:186](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:186) The existing-hook residual provides no effective mitigation: `.claude/settings.json` executes worker-writable `scripts/agent-stop-gate.sh`, while formatting runs PATH-resolved Prettier against worker-controlled JavaScript configuration; protecting `.claude` settings does not bind the executed code. .orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-987865d.md:2018:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:80](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:80) Remote SHA pinning and `--no-replace-objects` do not authenticate the writable object database: replacing an intermediate tree object can redirect ledger lookup to an attacker’s valid blob because that traversal does not verify the intermediate object’s content hash. .orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-f1b862c.md:14:Pre-dispatch security review (read-only, security profile) of the task text .orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md and its threat_table, before any implementation exists. End with exactly one line: Verdict: correct or Verdict: incorrect.

.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8bac9e5.md:3982:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:169](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:169) Verbatim argv forwarding permits `gh repo clone … -- --config core.sshCommand=<worker executable>` to execute worker code outside the Linux sandbox; fixed binaries and alias-free configuration do not close this path, and the named alias test never exercises it. [gh forwarding](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_repo_clone), [Git configuration timing](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-clone).

[Hook authority](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#security-considerations), [shim resolution](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/shims.html).

.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-f589c7c.md:1771:- 2026-10-19T03:24:11Z: C-80 review of the text (`.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8bac9e5.md`): `Verdict: incorrect`, seven P1, one P2: (1) the gh wrapper forwards argv verbatim, so `gh repo clone … -- --config core.sshCommand=<exe>` runs worker code outside the sandbox → the wrapper allows an explicit subcommand list and refuses `--` passthrough and config-carrying forms; (2) a bash wrapper reads BASH_ENV before `env -i` (probe confirmed) → the wrapper is Python under an absolute `-I` interpreter path rendered from the trusted root; (3) project hooks execute the worktree's `.claude/hooks/contextdb_hook.py` through bare `python3` and the format hooks resolve tools through shims → worker seats run no project hooks (a factual check of the settings switch is pending with the Claude Code docs); (4) Codex workers share `.git/objects` and `.git/refs` writes (herdr-agents:439), so `origin/main` can be replaced after a fetch → design 5.14 item 8 now binds the committed ledger to the sha `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` returns (amended 03:2xZ); (5) `git ls-tree` enumeration needs the sanitized git environment; (6) the reviewer states Edit deny rules also enter the Bash sandbox configuration, which would block the orchestrator's sandboxed record writes under `.orchestration/**` → a factual check pending; (7) `failIfUnavailable: false` lets a seat run unsandboxed when Linux dependencies are missing → `true` for worker seats; (8) P2: symlink and case-alias identity tests missing. .orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-519afd7.md:2733:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:273](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:273) The race acceptance rests on a false premise: a sandboxed worker can swap an allowed directory for a symlink after validation, causing the unsandboxed file tool to overwrite a trusted path that the worker cannot write directly; static path tests cannot close this boundary.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-519afd7.md:2735:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:80](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:80) Remote SHA pinning and `--no-replace-objects` do not authenticate the writable object database: replacing an intermediate tree object can redirect ledger lookup to an attacker’s valid blob because that traversal does not verify the intermediate object’s content hash. [Git tree traversal](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.51.0/tree-walk.c), [object reading](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.51.0/odb.c).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-519afd7.md:2737:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:219](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:219) Absolute hook entrypoints do not bind their descendants: retained `herdr-agent-state.sh:25` invokes bare `python3`, while delivery invokes scripts with `/usr/bin/env bash` shebangs; the specified launcher captures and tracked-hook tests miss these unsandboxed, PATH-resolved executions on this shim-first host. [Mise shim resolution](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/shims.html).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-519afd7.md:2739:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:84](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:84) The table omits the retained Herdr socket capability (`agent-config.yaml:325`): a sandboxed client can request terminal execution through the host server, whose existing driver uses `pane run`; refusing excluded command names does not restrict socket RPCs or the resulting host execution. [Unix-socket escape risk](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#security-limitations).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-519afd7.md:2741:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:275](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:275) Startup validation does not mitigate a later hook timeout or termination, which permits the protected action; Python exit-2 tests therefore leave enforcement fail-open, although Claude provides runtime-level `onFailure: "block"` starting with v2.1.295. [Hook failure control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#block-the-action-when-a-hook-fails).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-519afd7.md:2746:Verdict: incorrect- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:131](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:131) No threat row or control separates worker GitHub credentials from the orchestrator’s: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` does not isolate gh authentication, so a worker with the shared credential can call the merge API through permitted sandbox networking; GitHub cannot enforce the claimed seat identity distinction. [gh credential selection](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_environment).
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-519afd7.md:2748:- [P1] High confidence [.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:165](~/Workspace/dotfiles/.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01.md:165) The deny inventory trusts the same worker-writable Git objects and refs rejected for ledger authority: planted replacement refs can make `git ls-tree` omit protected paths, and neither `env -i` nor the prescribed flags authenticate that enumeration; the named fixtures omit this attack. # AGMSG-TASK dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01 — INV-6 reset of a01 on tools/worker-write-boundary-a01, seat a010; plan 024 P1-15 under D-024-17, D-024-19, D-024-20, D-024-21 and D-024-23

## Goal

This is the amendment-1 text of the task dispatched at 2026-10-19T05:42Z (the ninth-round text that passed its pre-dispatch security review). Amendment 1 folds in two interpretation notes the worker needed (the inherited make format clause; the portable tracked `.claude/settings.json` with host-specific paths only in the rendered guard) and removes the Codex worker profile item (a Codex seat edits no Codex-boundary source; it becomes the separate Claude-seat task dotfiles-T133-codex-worker-network-a01). Everything else is the dispatched text in meaning; the branch, the eight green tests and the fixtures stay; the worker swaps the task copy to this text at its next push.

The host is not a security boundary between seats sharing one OS user. gh keys Keychain credentials by host and user, so a worker running as the same macOS user can read the orchestrator's token regardless of `GH_CONFIG_DIR`. Prevention of a worker-initiated merge requires a separate OS user or host under D-024-23's future P1-16, which the operator decides whether to pursue. Until then the GitHub boundary is detection, not prevention. The regime detects missing acceptance or gate-passage evidence in the next records PR, not at main-push time, because the records reach main only with that boundary PR. On a PR touching `.orchestration/acceptance/**`, the regime job checks every main merge commit since the previous boundary for its corresponding acceptance record with gate-passage evidence and fails the PR when one is missing. P1-11 owns implementation of that check; this task states section 5.14 item 0's detection rule. Approvals and gate evidence of record are read from GitHub at a SHA through its API inside the sandbox. Host-local controls reduce accidental and injected damage without establishing isolation from a malicious same-UID process.

This task implements section 5.14 items 1, 9 and 10 through a dedicated Claude worker configuration directory, static Edit deny rules on trusted paths and worktree configuration, managed sandbox enforcement, guarded project hooks, hook interpreter and PATH bindings, private worker caches and the rule that worker commands run inside their sandbox. Every Claude seat has `sandbox.failIfUnavailable: true`.

The administrative managed policy is shared by every Claude seat. Its Herdr socket allowance and three control-plane exclusions remain available to workers as well as the orchestrator. Empty arrays in worker user settings do not subtract these managed entries. Their availability is a residual under item 0, and the worker execution rule supplies no authorization to use them outside the sandbox.

[memory:decision] D-024-20 makes this task the dispatch prerequisite of P1-14 a05, P1-10 a02, audit-pool-a02 and P1-6. The orchestrator places this task in their `after:` fields before dispatch. This task has `after: []`. A Codex seat performs these Claude configuration edits under the routing rule, including the Worker Playbook step 4 sentence permitted by plan 021 step 8.3. This Codex seat edits no Codex-boundary source.

The design source is `.orchestration/plans/024-design-quality.md` section 5.14 items 0 through 10. D-024-21, D-024-23 and the amended items 0, 1 and 8 govern this revision. D-024-22's proposed gh credential separation is superseded. The acceptance record preserves documentation facts and earlier proposals as history.

The third C-80 text review is `.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-ecc7ab5.md.last.md`. Its five P1 findings remain recorded. The retained mechanisms are documented symlink-aware deny rules, approval reads outside the local object database, hook interpreter bindings and runtime hook failure policy.

The fourth C-80 text review is `.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-8d42532.md.last.md`. Its six P1 findings remain recorded. The retained mechanisms are the static manifest deny inventory, protection of the orchestrator worklog and cache, narrow home denies around writable agmsg stores, correct linked-worktree hook placement and fixed hook-runtime PATH.

The fifth C-80 text review is `.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-worker-write-boundary-a01-text-security-08e6ac7.md.last.md`. Its three P1 findings remain recorded. This revision removes the gh credential-separation mechanism, records the upstream agmsg store-driver residual and moves sandbox enforcement into administrative managed settings.

The file-tool rule is the documented sentence, “Deny rules: apply when either the requested path or the file it resolves to matches.” Edit and Write refuse a requested file that is itself a symlink. Directory symlinks are subject to resolved-target permission checks, and the tools check the resolved location again when opening the approved file. These documented checks reduce redirection risk without establishing an atomic host security boundary against concurrent same-UID changes. [Claude permission reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#symlinks)

The 2026-10-19T03:45:06Z sandbox probe ran `gh api repos/mryfmo/dotfiles --jq .name` and returned `dotfiles`. The recorded sandbox proxy used CONNECT without TLS interception, and gh read the Keychain token. This historical observation confirms neither credential separation nor final-head deployment readiness.

The documentation facts recorded at 03:2xZ establish that Edit denies also affect the Bash sandbox, hooks reload during a session and an unavailable sandbox is fail-open by default. D-024-21's 04:0xZ decision establishes the dedicated Claude configuration mechanism, directory-specific Claude credentials, symlink coverage and `onFailure: "block"` support. These Claude credentials do not separate gh Keychain access.

The settings documentation states, “In a worktree, it uses the file at the main checkout’s root.” Linked-worktree sessions therefore load the main checkout's `.claude/settings.local.json`. Worker hooks belong in `~/.claude-worker/settings.json`, and the main checkout's local hooks also receive the orchestrator-only guard. [Claude local settings reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings#where-claude-code-keeps-the-local-file-in-a-git-repository)

## Files

1. `home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml` remains the source of agent policy and model profiles.

   The manifest names `orchestrator_checkout` as the anchored primary checkout and supplies trusted deployment bindings for the guard, hook scripts and absolute interpreters. These bindings resolve outside worker worktrees and executable caches. Worker cwd, tool input, worktree configuration and inherited command variables do not select them. The manifest also supplies the trusted bindings from which the render resolves the absolute directories holding `ruff`, `prettier` and `terminal-browser`, without using mise shims.

   The manifest defines a separate Claude worker settings output at `home/.chezmoitemplates/claude-worker-settings.json` and an administrative managed-settings output at `home/.chezmoitemplates/claude-managed-settings.json`. The worker configuration directory is `~/.claude-worker`. The launcher passes its expanded absolute path as `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.

   A static `trusted_paths:` list names every protected top-level path of the anchored checkout and the protected home paths. It explicitly includes `<anchored-checkout>/.agents/worklog/**` and `<anchored-checkout>/.agents/worklog/uv-cache/**`. The `.claude` entries protect tracked contents and the main checkout's `.claude/settings.local.json` without denying the whole `.claude/worktrees/` tree. The list explicitly names directory targets and descendant patterns where both are required.

   Separate worker Edit denies protect `//<anchored-checkout>/.claude/worktrees/*/.claude/**` and `//<anchored-checkout>/.claude/worktrees/*/.mcp.json`. The `.claude` directory target is also protected. Ordinary worktree source files and the per-seat cache remain outside these configuration denies.

   The home-path denies are `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml`, `~/.agents/model-profiles.env`, `~/.agents/skills/**/scripts/**`, `~/.agents/skills/**/SKILL.md`, `~/.agents/skills/agmsg/plugins/**`, `~/.agents/skills/agmsg/db/trusted-plugins`, `~/.claude/**`, `~/.claude-worker/**`, `~/.local/bin/**`, `~/.local/share/**`, `~/.local/state/**`, `~/.local/share/mise/**`, `~/.config/**`, `~/.cache/uv/**` and `~/.local/share/uv/**`. No blanket deny on `~/.agents/**` or `~/.local/**` replaces this list.

# OpenAI Docs

Provide current, cited OpenAI product, API, model, and Codex guidance. Read zero or one primary reference.

**First substantive action:** Search the user's exact requested official OpenAI documentation topic and any explicitly named model using a concise, topic-specific query of 2-6 essential terms. When an already-available direct official documentation search and page-retrieval capability is present, use it first: search, then fetch or open the matching official page before general web search. Otherwise, immediately use official-domain web search, then actually open or fetch the relevant official page. Complete this source order before reading a reference, inspecting local or repository files, running a Codex manual or model resolver, drafting a plan, or answering from memory. Use the actual fetched page, not a search snippet or an unopened link. If one official search or page does not establish the answer, search another appropriate official domain and actually open or fetch the result. Preserve the exact requested model; never substitute a newer model.

**Only exception:** An explicitly requested, genuinely broad, cross-topic Codex setup, orientation, or system-map synthesis may use the manual first when shell execution and an allowed temporary cache are available. A specific Codex feature, setting, command, error, model, or requested citation remains docs-first. Mixed Chat/Work/Codex comparisons are official documentation questions, not manual-first Codex requests.

For generic software tasks, answer the software task directly. OpenAI implementation, debugging, SDK, API, prompting, agent, and eval requests are not generic.

For a straightforward factual or citation-only request, follow the source order and do not read a route reference. This includes straightforward API facts, ChatGPT Work or mixed Chat/Work/Codex comparisons, model tiers, aliases, Pro mode, reasoning settings, factual migration baselines, and narrow Codex facts. Prioritize `learn.chatgpt.com` for ChatGPT Work.

## Choose one primary route

Use the first matching route, and read its reference only when the requested task needs that specialized workflow:

- **Explicitly requested local documentation integration:** Read [integration guidance](references/mcp-diagnostics.md) only when the user explicitly requests that local integration.
- **Model migration, upgrades, or model-specific prompting:** Read [model-migration.md](references/model-migration.md) for actual migration planning, implementation, dynamic target resolution, or prompt changes. Preserve an explicitly requested target.
- **Model selection and comparisons:** Read [model-selection.md](references/model-selection.md) only when nuanced current, latest, default, cost, latency, quality, or modality tradeoffs need more guidance. Do not run a migration resolver for selection alone.
- **Product, API, ChatGPT Work, and mixed Chat/Work/Codex documentation:** Read [official-docs.md](references/official-docs.md) only when fetched official pages leave source selection, API schemas, or the requested implementation unresolved. This route is not manual-first.
- **Explicitly broad Codex setup, orientation, or cross-topic synthesis:** Read [codex-self-knowledge.md](references/codex-self-knowledge.md) when the eligible Codex manual or deeper Codex procedures are needed.

Read at most one primary reference. Do not open every route, bundled model guide, or helper script. Read a supporting reference or run a helper only when the chosen workflow demonstrably needs it.

## Source and execution boundaries

- Search, open, fetch, and cite only `developers.openai.com`, `platform.openai.com`, and `learn.chatgpt.com`. Cite the page that supports the claim. State uncertainty when official sources do not establish pricing, availability, account access, limits, or behavior.
- Preserve an explicitly requested model for selection, migration, and prompting. Resolve an unspecified latest or current migration target only after searching and fetching current official guidance.
- Use `references/latest-model.md` only as a disclosed fallback after current official model guidance does not answer the question. Read `references/upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md` only for an actual, requested GPT-6 migration; read `references/prompting-guide.md` only for requested prompting work.
- Before building, running, editing, debugging, or testing an API-backed app or tool, use `openai-platform-api-key` first when available. Documentation, conceptual examples, model selection, and read-only guidance do not require an API key.
- Say "OpenAI Docs" or "official OpenAI documentation" in user-facing answers. Keep exact official citations and examples concise.

2. **無害化した環境を最初に** 最初の処理として `env -i` に入り、PATH は信頼ルートで解決した絶対バイナリへのリンクだけの私設ディレクトリ（shims、空、相対は拒否）。git は毎回 `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false -c protocol.allow=never -c protocol.https.allow=always` と明示 `-C`（https だけ許す。`protocol.allow=never` 単独は必要な fetch を止める）。 検査の読み取りは `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` で部分クローンの遅延 fetch（checkout 設定の credential.helper を起動しうる）を止め、`-c submodule.recurse=false --ignore-submodules=all` で submodule 内の status/diff（submodule 自身の設定が filter を有効化しうる）を止める。`.gitmodules` を持つ checkout は検査対象として拒否する。 `-C` は作業木を束縛しないので（repo-local の `core.worktree` が読み先を checkout 外へ向けられる）、git は `--git-dir=<checkout>/.git --work-tree=<checkout>` を明示し、`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` の realpath が checkout と一致しないときは拒否する。 premise や検査の「コマンド実行」は、固定語彙の読み取り専用プローブ（`git rev-parse <ref>`、`test -e <path>`、`grep -c <pattern> <file>` のように検査器自身が解釈する形）だけを許し、任意のシェル文字列は実行しない（本文のハッシュはコマンド文を認証するだけで、`python -I scripts/x.py` のファイル被演算子や `source ./x.sh` の中身は認証しない）。diff と show は `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv` と `-c core.attributesFile=/dev/null -c core.sshCommand=false` を付け、PR 側の `.gitattributes`（external diff、textconv、filter）が検査内容や実行物を変えないようにする。Python は `-I`。PATH 探索で実行するものは無い。
3. **信頼パスの境界検査** 仕組みが信頼するパス（スクリプト、台帳、証跡、worktree、lock、出力先）は realpath で解決し、`.claude/worktrees/` または manifest の worker ルート配下なら拒否（ask/hold）。symlink 構成要素は解決後に比較し、大小文字を区別しないファイルシステムでは同一性比較を大小文字非依存で行う。
4. **検証したものを実行し、検証した内容を渡す** 検証した実行体はその realpath で実行する（再探索しない）。検証したファイル内容は信頼ルート配下のスナップショット（0600、一意名）として渡し、使用直前に sha256 を再照合する。判断に読んだ証跡は sha256 を出力に記録する。
5. **出力と予約の同一性** 名前には 40 桁の head を使う（7 桁で衝突させない）。lock は信頼ルート配下の固定 inode に O_EXCL で作り、置換を inode 比較で検出する。物理スロット 1 つに lock 1 つ。
6. **正直な残余** 境界だけが緩和するリスクを `closed` と書かない。各文は残余を 1 行で明記する。
0. **脅威モデル（D-024-21）** 席は同じ OS ユーザで動き、ホストは席間の信頼境界ではない（同一 UID のプロセスは symlink 差し替え、共有 `.git` の object 差し替え、hook の子プロセス、Herdr socket 経由の host 実行で、ホスト内のどの検査も迂回できる）。regime の硬い境界は GitHub（保護された main、必須チェック、orchestrator の identity によるマージ）。ただしこの境界は **worker 席が orchestrator の GitHub 資格情報を共有しない**ときだけ成立する（D-024-22：worker 席は専用の GitHub identity（別アカウントまたは App のトークン）で `gh` に login し、ruleset の bypass 一覧に入らない。orchestrator の keychain トークンを worker の config dir に持ち込まない。identity が分かれるまで「GitHub が境界」は未成立と書く）。**同一 macOS ユーザでは資格情報は分離できない**（gh は keychain の項目を host/user で引き、同じ UID の gh は orchestrator のトークンを読める。`GH_CONFIG_DIR` は設定を分けるだけ）。防止には worker 席を別の OS ユーザ（または別ホスト）で動かすしかなく、それは D-024-23 の将来項目（P1-16、操作者の判断）。それまで GitHub 境界は **検知**で守る：記録は boundary の記録 PR まで main に無いので、検知は次の記録 PR の regime ジョブで行う（`.orchestration/acceptance/**` に触れる PR で、前回 boundary 以降の main の各マージ commit に、gate 通過の証跡を持つ受け入れ記録が対応することを検査し、無ければその PR を失敗させる；P1-11 owner a02 の行 `ci:detection:1`）。main push 時点の検知は記録が無いので不可能であり、文は「次の記録 PR で検知、防止ではない」と書く。悪意ある worker に耐えるべき入力（承認台帳、gate が読む証跡 of record）は GitHub から sha 指定で API 経由（sandbox 内）に読み、ローカルファイルやローカル object database からは読まない。ホスト内の制御（本節 1〜10）は事故と prompt injection による損害の抑制であり、文はそう書く。
8. **承認はコミット済み台帳から読む** permission の決定行（`scope=permission approved_by=user diff_sha256=…`）は anchored checkout の作業コピーではなく、コミット済みの台帳から読む。読み方は `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` が返す commit sha を取り、GitHub API（`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/.orchestration/decisions.tsv?ref=<sha>`、sandbox 内）でその sha の内容を取得する。ローカルの `git show` は共有 object database が書けるため中間 tree の差し替えで偽物を返しうる（第 3 回審査の所見 2）（ローカルの ref 名 `origin/main` は経由しない。`refs/replace/` も書けるので replacement を無効にする。Codex worker は `.git/objects` と `.git/refs` に書けるので ref は差し替えられるが、sha で指した object は内容アドレスで偽造できない）。作業コピーの行は提案で、記録 PR が main にマージされて初めて承認になる（PR の承認は操作者の操作）。偽造には main へのマージが要る。

def claude_skill_symlink_outputs() -> dict[Path, str]:
    outputs: dict[Path, str] = {}
    skills_root = ROOT / "home/dot_agents/skills"
    claude_root = ROOT / "home/dot_claude/skills"
    if not skills_root.exists():
        return outputs
    for source_file in sorted(path for path in skills_root.rglob("*") if path.is_file()):
        if source_file.name.startswith("."):
            continue
        rel = source_file.relative_to(skills_root)
        target_path = rel.with_name(chezmoi_target_name(rel.name))
        target_dir = claude_root / target_path.parent
        outputs[target_dir / f"symlink_{target_path.name}.tmpl"] = render_claude_skill_symlink(source_file)
    return outputs


def render_codex_profile(name: str, profile: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    codex = profile["codex"]
    lines = [
        f'# Codex model profile "{name}"; launch with: codex --profile {name}',
        f"# {GENERATED_HEADER}",
        "",
        f"model = {quote_toml(codex['model'])}",
        f"model_reasoning_effort = {quote_toml(codex['model_reasoning_effort'])}",
    ]
    # Overrides the global sandbox_mode; profiles without it inherit the base config.
    if sandbox_mode := codex.get("sandbox_mode"):
        lines.append(f"sandbox_mode = {quote_toml(sandbox_mode)}")
    if notify := codex.get("notify"):
        lines.append(f"notify = {quote_toml(notify)}")
    lines.extend(
        [
            "",
            "[features]",
            "hooks = true",
            "",
            "[hooks.state]",
        ]
    )
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


HOOK_TRUST_BEGIN = "# >>> codex hook trust (generated by scripts/generate-agent-configs.py; edit it there) >>>\n"
HOOK_TRUST_END = "# <<< codex hook trust <<<\n"
# Apply-time Codex hook trust, shared by the base and profile modify scripts. Codex runs a config or
# plugin hook only when [hooks.state."<key>"] holds the trust hash of its current definition, and that
# hash covers the absolute command path, so it is computed on each host from the hook it names.
HOOK_TRUST_CODE = """import functools
import hashlib
import json
import re

HOOK_TRUST_HOME = "{{ .chezmoi.homeDir }}"
NO_MATCHER_HOOK_EVENTS = frozenset({"user_prompt_submit", "stop", "interrupt"})
SHORT_TIMEOUT_HOOK_EVENTS = frozenset({"session_end", "interrupt"})


def hook_event_label(event: str) -> str:
            {
                "matcher": "*",
                "hooks": [
                    {
                        "type": "command",
                        "command": hook["command"],
                        "timeout": hook["timeout"],
                        "statusMessage": hook["status_message"],
                    }
                ],
            }
        )
    declared = []
    for key, state in hooks.get("state", {}).items():
        if not isinstance(state, dict) or set(state) - {"trusted_hash", "enabled"}:
            fail(f"codex.hooks.state.{key} may only set trusted_hash and enabled")
        declared.append({"key": key, **state})
    return {"declared": declared, "config_hooks": config_hooks}


def render_hook_trust_block(manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    return HOOK_TRUST_BEGIN + f"HOOK_TRUST = {codex_hook_trust(manifest)!r}\n" + HOOK_TRUST_CODE + HOOK_TRUST_END


def render_codex_base_modify(manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """The hand-maintained base modify script with its generated hook-trust block refreshed."""
    relative = "home/dot_codex/modify_private_config.toml"
    # A fixture ROOT (unit tests) has no base script of its own; take the repository's copy then.
    source = ROOT / relative if (ROOT / relative).exists() else Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / relative
    text = source.read_text()
    start, end = text.find(HOOK_TRUST_BEGIN), text.find(HOOK_TRUST_END)
    if start == -1 or end < start:
        fail("home/dot_codex/modify_private_config.toml must keep the codex hook trust block markers")
    return text[:start] + render_hook_trust_block(manifest) + text[end + len(HOOK_TRUST_END) :]


def render_codex_profile_modify(name: str, profile: dict[str, Any], manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    managed = render_codex_profile(name, profile)
    render_helper = ""
    managed_source = "MANAGED"
    if "{{ .chezmoi.homeDir }}" in managed:
        render_helper = """\n\ndef render_managed_paths(text: str) -> str:
    return text.replace("{{ .chezmoi.homeDir }}", str(Path.home()))
"""
        managed_source = "render_managed_paths(MANAGED)"
    return f'''#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Merge the managed Codex {name} profile with Codex-owned runtime state."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path
import re

RUNTIME_PREFIXES = {RUNTIME_PREFIXES!r}
MANAGED = {managed!r}
{render_helper}
__HOOK_TRUST_BLOCK__

def table_name(header: str) -> str | None:
    """The raw name of a `[table]` or `[[array]]` header line, which may end in a `# comment`, else None."""
    stripped = header.strip()
    if not stripped.startswith("["):
        return None
    double = stripped.startswith("[[")
    start = index = 2 if double else 1
    quote = None
    while index < len(stripped):
        char = stripped[index]
        if quote == '"' and char == "\\\\":
            index += 2
            continue
        if char == quote:
            quote = None
        elif quote is None and char in ('"', "'"):
            quote = char
        elif quote is None and char == "]":
            break
        index += 1
    else:
        return None

Amendment 1 folds in two interpretation notes the worker needed (the inherited make format clause; the portable tracked `.claude/settings.json` with host-specific paths only in the rendered guard) and removes the Codex worker profile item (a Codex seat edits no Codex-boundary source; it becomes the separate Claude-seat task dotfiles-T133-codex-worker-network-a01). 167-
168-The host is not a security boundary between seats sharing one OS user. gh keys Keychain credentials by host and user, so a worker running as the same macOS user can read the orchestrator's token regardless of `GH_CONFIG_DIR`. Prevention of a worker-initiated merge requires a separate OS user or host under D-024-23's future P1-16, which the operator decides whether to pursue. Until then the GitHub boundary is detection, not prevention. The regime detects missing acceptance or gate-passage evidence in the next records PR, not at main-push time, because the records reach main only with that boundary PR. On a PR touching `.orchestration/acceptance/**`, the regime job checks every main merge commit since the previous boundary for its corresponding acceptance record with gate-passage evidence and fails the PR when one is missing. P1-11 owns implementation of that check; this task states section 5.14 item 0's detection rule. Approvals and gate evidence of record are read from GitHub at a SHA through its API inside the sandbox. Host-local controls reduce accidental and injected damage without establishing isolation from a malicious same-UID process.

184-The file-tool rule is the documented sentence, “Deny rules: apply when either the requested path or the file it resolves to matches.” Edit and Write refuse a requested file that is itself a symlink. Directory symlinks are subject to resolved-target permission checks, and the tools check the resolved location again when opening the approved file. These documented checks reduce redirection risk without establishing an atomic host security boundary against concurrent same-UID changes. [Claude permission reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#symlinks)

def split_chunks(text: str) -> list[tuple[str | None, str]]:
    chunks: list[tuple[str | None, str]] = []
    current_name: str | None = None
    current_lines: list[str] = []
    pending_lines: list[str] = []
    string = None
    for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
        # A header-like line inside a multiline string is string content, never a chunk boundary.
        name = table_name(line) if string is None else None
        string = multiline_string_after(line, string)
        if name is None:
            if current_name is None:
                pending_lines.append(line)
            else:
                current_lines.append(line)
            continue
        if current_name is None:
            if pending_lines:
                split_at = len(pending_lines)
                while split_at and not pending_lines[split_at - 1].strip():
                    split_at -= 1
                if split_at:
                    chunks.append((None, "".join(pending_lines[:split_at])))
                pending_lines = pending_lines[split_at:]
        else:
            chunks.append((current_name, "".join(current_lines)))
        current_name = name
        current_lines = pending_lines + [line]
        pending_lines = []
    if current_name is None:
        if pending_lines:
            chunks.append((None, "".join(pending_lines)))
    else:
        chunks.append((current_name, "".join(current_lines)))
    return chunks


def runtime_prefix(name: str | None) -> str | None:
    if name is None:
        return None
    for prefix in RUNTIME_PREFIXES:
        if name == prefix or name.startswith(f"{{prefix}}."):
            return prefix
    return None


def base_hook_state() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Harvest operator-granted hook trust from the base Codex config."""
    path = Path.home() / ".codex/config.toml"
    if not path.is_file():
        return []
    return [
        (name, chunk)
        for name, chunk in split_chunks(path.read_text())
        if runtime_prefix(name) == "hooks.state"
    ]


def trusted_hash(chunk: str) -> str | None:
    """Parse a persisted hook-trust hash without recalculating or trusting it."""
    match = re.search(r'^trusted_hash = "([^"]+)"$', chunk, re.MULTILINE)
    return match.group(1) if match else None
